annotations.text:
Retail dashboard — 5 directions
Same data (Ama Serwaa, GHS 18,450.00 available), five different organizing ideas: hero number, account carousel, forecast-first, task-first, activity feed. Built on the app's real tokens (Geist, zero-bold, oklch blue, rounded-2xl) — not the old GCB portal's layout, just its functional coverage.

Full feature coverage
AccountsHub and PaymentsHub are what 'View all' / 'Pay bill' lead to from every lean concept above — loans, term deposits, favorites, billers and standing instructions all live here, one tap away. Below, MainComplete and CarouselComplete are the same two concepts with that depth pulled onto the home screen face instead, so you can compare lean vs. complete directly.

Wise & Wealthsimple directions
These three sit inside the app's REAL shell — the actual sidebar and floating card from CustomerShell.tsx, not a page-content mockup. WiseWallet borrows the stacked-card account presentation and pill actions. WealthsimpleChart borrows the trend-chart hero and a genuine privacy blur. Hybrid combines the two strongest mechanisms — the stacked wallet card and the rotating offer rail — while staying chart-free and lean.

Skrill directions
Skrill is single-wallet, so its balance-panel-plus-three-square-actions pattern needed a genuine adaptation for multi-account NIBS, not a straight copy: SkrillSwitcher puts an account picker inside the panel; SkrillStacked repeats the bold panel in miniature for your top two accounts; SkrillRail keeps one aggregate total and moves individual accounts to a chip rail underneath. All three also borrow Skrill's constrained centered content column instead of full-bleed. Left out on purpose: Skrill's sports-betting and casino promo widgets — not appropriate for a bank.

Second state — Loan selected
What 'switching accounts' actually has to do: the three square actions stop being Add / Transfer / Pay bill (none of which make sense for a loan) and become Make a payment / View schedule / Statement. The chart becomes a repayment progress bar instead of a spend trend. Transactions filter to loan repayments only. SkrillSwitcherLoan sits under the Switcher concept, SkrillRailLoan under the Rail concept — same rule, two affordances.

Where do cards live on SkrillRail?
Five answers to the gap flagged earlier: none of the Skrill concepts showed cards anywhere but the sidebar nav link. A — a fifth chip in the rail, set off by a divider. B — a lean inline link next to Balance, count only, no status. C — a full dedicated panel, most visible, costs the most space. D — contextual: cards only appear once an account that has them is selected (shown here with Current active), invisible on the aggregate view. E — a fourth square action alongside Add/Transfer/Pay bill.

Option F — Wise touch
Requested after seeing A-E: bring Wise's stacked-card visual into the winner. F takes Option C's full panel and redraws the two cards as an actual layered deck — real card art (masked number, holder name, expiry, network mark), the physical Visa in front, the virtual GCB card peeking behind with a 'Virtual' badge — with the plain status list kept underneath so nothing from C is lost, just made to look like a card instead of a settings row.

This is what actually shipped
Not a mockup — recreated from the real components (LiquidityRail, CardsStack, AnalyticsPreview, the real sidebar shell) and the real data currently rendering at /overview. The account rail shows Current and Savings only: the Account model has no Loan or Term Deposit type, so — as discussed — there's no chip to add. Primary actions are Send money / Top up / Quick pay, not Add / Transfer / Pay bill, matching this app's own documented frequency ordering rather than the Skrill mockup's labels. FX rates is gone from this page entirely; it already has its own place in the sidebar.

Figma redesign, fixed — retail and corporate
Starts from the Figma frame's list-row account pattern (node 391:12378) rather than replacing it — it genuinely scales better than a pill rail once a relationship has 3+ accounts. Fixes applied: balance and accounts merged into one card instead of a separate boxed panel; rows filter the page (tap-to-select, matching the shipped rail) instead of navigating away; each account shows its own correct balance (the Figma frame duplicated one number across both rows); dropped the mismatched US flag on a GHS account; Analytics numbers are real formatted money, not bare integers; cut the 5-tab time-range switcher from the home glance (that's exploration, moved to Reports) and paired Cards with Analytics side-by-side to cut scroll depth; card stack shows the 2 real cards, not 3.

RedesignRetail is Ama Serwaa's 2-account view. RedesignCorporate is the same layout under load: Efua Mensah (Approver) at Adinkra Textiles Ltd, 3 real accounts, a 4th 'Bulk pay' square action, and the 'Requires your attention' approvals band actually rendering in the slot AsBuilt's placeholder only reserved — same component order, no rework needed to go from one profile to the other.

Half-and-half — from the shared Figma frame (node 5586:140)
That frame splits the page into two functional columns instead of one: money on the left (balance, accounts, cards, activity), act-and-understand on the right (Quick Actions, Analytics). This iteration keeps that split - it's a genuinely different organizing idea, not just a restyle - and carries over the same fixes as the other two: accounts merged with the balance rather than boxed separately, each row its own correct balance (the Figma frame had the same duplicated 'GH₵ GH₵18,070.50' bug), Analytics as real formatted money with no time-range tabs. Two changes specific to this direction: the three square actions move out of the balance card entirely into their own 'Quick actions' panel (4 actions, since there's finally room), and the promotional 'Ad' block at the bottom of the right column was dropped rather than recreated - a house ad slot on a banking dashboard wasn't something to fabricate, and no ad content was supplied.

5 ways to present the accounts
Same data, same balance panel and actions on every artboard — only the accounts section changes, so these compare cleanly. A — Refined rows: this session's direction, tightened: a left accent bar replaces the boxed border, balance right-aligned. B — Tiles: both balances always visible, zero taps — closest to Concept 1, costs the most vertical space at 2 accounts. C — Horizontal scroll cards: identical shape at 2 accounts or 12, touch-friendly, hides accounts off-screen until swiped. D — Inline segmented switch: the whole accounts section collapses into the balance header as a 3-way toggle plus a 'Show details' disclosure — the most compact, but buries the numbers a tap deeper. E — Dense ledger table: account/number/status/balance as real columns, most information per pixel, reads as ops tooling rather than a consumer balance — the one built for corporate scale, not retail's 2 accounts.
